title: Financial statements and the reporting entity
summary: The objective and scope of financial statements, the reporting period, perspective, going concern, and what a reporting entity and consolidated statements are.

chunks.heading: Objective and scope of financial statements
chunks.explanation_md:
Chapters 1 and 2 are about general purpose financial **reports**. Chapters 3 to 8 are about general purpose financial **statements**, a particular form of report. Statements give information about the entity's economic resources, claims against it and changes in them, **in terms of the elements** (assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses).

**Objective:** to give financial information about the entity's **assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses** that is useful to users in assessing the prospects for **future net cash inflows** and **management's stewardship**.

The information is provided:

- in the **statement of financial position**, by recognising assets, liabilities and equity;
- in the **statement(s) of financial performance**, by recognising income and expenses; and
- in **other statements and notes**, by presenting and disclosing: recognised items (their nature and risks); **unrecognised** assets and liabilities (nature and risks); **cash flows**; **contributions from and distributions to holders of equity claims**; and the **methods, assumptions and judgements** used in estimates and changes in them.
chunks.exam_line: Financial statements provide information on assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses through the statement of financial position, the statement(s) of financial performance, and other statements and notes.

chunks.heading: Reporting period, perspective and going concern
chunks.explanation_md:
**Reporting period.** Statements cover a specified period. They give information on assets, liabilities and equity (including unrecognised ones) **at the end of, or during**, the period, and on **income and expenses for the period**. To help users spot changes and trends, they also give **comparative information for at least one preceding period**.

**Forward-looking information** is included only if it relates to the entity's assets, liabilities, equity, income or expenses at the end of or during the period **and** is useful to users. For example, if a measure uses estimated future cash flows, information about those estimates may help. Statements do **not** usually include other forward-looking material such as management's expectations and strategies. They include events **after** the period end only if needed to meet their objective.

**Perspective.** Statements view transactions from the perspective of the **reporting entity as a whole**, not from any one group of investors, lenders or creditors.

**Going concern.** Statements are normally prepared assuming the entity is a **going concern** and will continue for the **foreseeable future**: it has neither the intention nor the need to liquidate or stop trading. If it does, the statements may have to be prepared on a different basis, and they **describe the basis used**.

key_terms.meaning: The assumption that the entity will continue in operation for the foreseeable future, with no intention or need to liquidate or cease trading.

chunks.exam_line: Statements cover a reporting period with comparatives for at least one earlier period, view the entity as a whole, and assume going concern unless the entity must liquidate or stop trading.

chunks.heading: The reporting entity
chunks.explanation_md:
A **reporting entity** is an entity that is **required, or chooses, to prepare financial statements**. It may be a single entity, **a portion of an entity**, or **more than one entity**. It is **not necessarily a legal entity**.

- If a **parent** controls a **subsidiary** and the reporting entity covers both, the statements are **consolidated**.
- If the reporting entity is the parent alone, the statements are **unconsolidated**.
- If it covers two or more entities that are **not all linked** by a parent-subsidiary relationship, the statements are **combined**.

**Boundary.** Fixing the boundary can be hard when the entity is not a legal entity and is not just a parent and subsidiaries. Then the boundary is driven by the **information needs of primary users**, who need relevant, faithful information. Faithful representation requires that the boundary: (a) is not an **arbitrary or incomplete** set of activities; (b) gives **neutral** information; and (c) comes with a **description of how it was set** and what the entity comprises.

chunks.heading: Consolidated and unconsolidated statements
chunks.explanation_md:
**Consolidated statements** report the assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses of the **parent and its subsidiaries as a single entity**. This helps investors and creditors of the parent judge its **prospects for net cash inflows**, because cash coming to the parent includes **distributions from subsidiaries**, which depend on the subsidiaries' own net cash inflows. They do **not** give separate information about a particular subsidiary; the subsidiary's own statements do that.

**Unconsolidated statements** give information about the **parent alone**. This is useful because (a) a claim against the parent **typically gives no claim against subsidiaries**, and (b) in some places the amounts that can be distributed to the parent's equity holders depend on the **parent's distributable reserves**. Information about the parent alone can also be given in the **notes** to consolidated statements.

Unconsolidated statements are **not enough** on their own, so **they cannot replace consolidated statements** when those are required. A parent may still be required, or choose, to prepare both.

key_terms.meaning: Statements of a reporting entity that is the parent alone.

questions.stem: Differentiate between consolidated, unconsolidated and combined financial statements.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Consolidated:** the reporting entity comprises a **parent and its subsidiaries**; the statements show their assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses as a single entity.

**Unconsolidated:** the reporting entity is the **parent alone**.

**Combined:** the reporting entity comprises **two or more entities not all linked by a parent-subsidiary relationship**.

Consolidated statements are needed because cash inflows to the parent include distributions from subsidiaries; unconsolidated statements cannot replace them when required.

questions.stem: Discuss the scope of general purpose financial statements: objective, reporting period, perspective, going concern and the reporting entity.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Objective.** General purpose financial statements are a form of general purpose report. They give information about the entity's **assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses** that is useful to assess prospects for **future net cash inflows** and **management's stewardship**. They do this through the **statement of financial position**, the **statement(s) of financial performance** and **other statements and notes** (recognised and unrecognised items, cash flows, contributions and distributions, and methods and judgements).

**Reporting period.** They cover a period and give **comparatives for at least one preceding period** so that users can see changes and trends. Forward-looking information is included only if it relates to items at or during the period and is useful, and events after the period are included if needed to meet the objective.

**Perspective.** The entity as a whole, not one group of investors or creditors.

**Going concern.** The statements assume the entity will continue for the foreseeable future; otherwise they use and describe a different basis.

**Reporting entity.** An entity required or choosing to prepare statements; it may be a single entity, a portion of an entity or several, and need not be a legal entity. Its boundary, where unclear, is set by the information needs of primary users and must not be arbitrary or incomplete, must give neutral information and must be described.
